Subject: Request: Private Plan license caps & rollback - Azure Marketplace

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement at StellarNet needs clarity on two items before we can route purchase:

1) License capacity and overage behavior — we need a clear rollback path if usage spikes are temporary (90-day rollback window).
2) Marketplace entitlements — can you confirm whether the private plan SKU supports entitlement adjustments mid-term and how refunds / invoice credits are handled?

Can you loop in whoever owns marketplace ops and legal? We want to avoid an open-ended credit exposure.

John — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Marissa (sales lead) and Ben (billing/ops).

High level from our side: we do support a 90-day usage lookback for one-time credits on hosted usage in exceptional cases; for Azure Private Plans there are two separate considerations: the marketplace entitlement (issuer-owned SKU) and the downstream billing reconciliation. On the legal side we usually handle rollback mechanics in a narrow DPA/Exhibit or an amendment to the private offer.

Marissa / Ben — can you confirm:
- whether we can expose a 90-day rollback clause in the private offer exhibit, and
- what the operational steps are to adjust entitlements mid-term and issue invoice credits (process, timeline, owner).

John — I can draft a short amendment for review once we confirm operations & legal language.

Thanks,
Rishi
Head of Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Rishi / John — quick read from sales: we can add a scoped rollback clause that allows one corrective entitlement adjustment within a 90-day window for clearly defined spike events (force majeure / pilot overshoot / known churn). That language will need two guardrails:

- A cap on total refundable amount (we recommend not exceeding 25% of the disputed invoice in the 90-day window), and
- A requirement for StellarNet to submit usage proof and a short RCA within 30 days of the spike.

Operationally, Ben will handle entitlement updates but we need Azure marketplace SKU re-issuance via the private offer flow; that typically takes 48-72 hours from our side once legal signs off.

Attaching a redline with suggested commercial language (redline_Azure_PrivatePlan_v2.docx).

Next steps: Rishi to confirm legal language and Ben to confirm billing matrix/timeline.

-Marissa

John/Team — operational notes from billing/ops:

1) Entitlement adjustments: we can adjust the private plan quantity in the marketplace entitlement but the marketplace invoice will still reflect the committed SKU for the billing period. For any refund/credit, we do a downstream credit memo on our invoice to StellarNet.

2) Timeline: once legal signs an amendment we can process entitlement update in 1-3 business days and then process a credit memo in the next billing cycle (commonly 7-10 business days after the change).

3) Documentation: please send usage exports (start/end timestamps + line item) to billing@redwood.ai. I'll validate and calculate a proportional credit per our agreed cap.

I attached a simple billing matrix (billing_matrix_stellarnet.xlsx) that maps scenarios to credit logic.

-ben
